name: Miguel Salazar
headline: Useful worlds for a life most alive.
intro: I turn ambiguous, human problems into products people can feel, understand, and use—combining product direction, research, design, and working software.
bio: My work moves between software, culture, health, and public-interest systems. I like overlooked problems, unusual references, and the moment a loose idea becomes something another person can actually touch. The thread is simple: make the stakes legible, keep the human texture, and prove what works.
availability: Open to unusual collaborations and consequential problems.
contactPrompt: Bring a hard problem, an early signal, or a world worth making real.

principles.title: Make ambiguity tangible
principles.body: A useful prototype gives a vague problem edges, stakes, and a place to test the next decision.

principles.title: Proof over posture
principles.body: A local build, a launch, and an outcome are different states. Name the state and show the evidence.

principles.title: Human stakes first
principles.body: Privacy, fear, access, dignity, and delight are product requirements—not copy added at the end.

principles.title: Keep the strange parts
principles.body: The memorable answer is rarely the most generic one. Preserve the detail that gives the work a pulse.
